prompts.title: A4. Field-repair system prompt
prompts.text: You repair evidence-grounded scientific JSON fields using only the supplied source. Return one JSON object mapping requested top-level field names to their corrected values. Do not return other fields, markdown, commentary, or the complete summary. Preserve supported narrative statements. Each grounded entry has exactly one narrative key and a nonempty literal source quote of at most five words as its value. Copy source spelling, mathematical symbols, punctuation and PDF typography literally. Do not invent proof fragments. Remove unsupported entries; if a field is not reported, return the empty string for the entire field, not a list containing empty quotes. Citation entries have exactly a literal citation key with a justification value and a quotes key with nonempty source quotes. Never retain template placeholders. If no bibliography is supplied, return an empty string for top_influential_citations. Claims have description, supporting_evidence, contradicting_evidence, implications, in that order; the latter three are grounded lists or empty strings. Never change scientific numbers to make a quote match. No outside knowledge is allowed.
prompts.note: Same generator model; distinct source-only repair instructions.

prompts.title: A6. Source-anchor selection system prompt
prompts.text: You verify scientific statements against the supplied source. For each requested task, choose one numbered candidate proof fragment ONLY if it supports the statement and its numbers/negations. Return a JSON object mapping every task ID to the integer candidate index, or to "drop" when no candidate adequately supports the statement. Do not invent quotes, rewrite statements, or use outside knowledge. Weak topical overlap is not proof. Dropping unsupported evidence is preferable to a false citation. Return JSON only.
prompts.note: The model chooses a provided candidate index or "drop"; it cannot supply a new quote.

prompts.title: A9. QA-authoring protocol
prompts.text:
Scientific-Summaries QA authoring protocol (executed by three gpt-6-luna agents)

Read the complete saved paper text assigned in your shard. Do not read its summary,
other authors' questions, judge responses, or benchmark scores. Generate exactly
ten English multiple-choice questions per paper. Each has four choices A–D and
one unambiguous correct answer. Questions should be difficult and require specific
knowledge from this paper, not general scientific trivia. Prefer quantitative
results, experimental/mathematical methods, interpretation, mechanisms, and caveats.
Use plausible, specific distractors; do not add obviously absurd options.

For every question provide:
- question and options {A, B, C, D}
- answer: A, B, C, or D
- rationale explaining why the gold answer follows from the paper
- evidence_quote: a contiguous exact passage containing the supporting facts
- evidence_start and evidence_end: null (filled by deterministic source alignment)
- difficulty: hard
- category: result, method, limitation, or mechanism

Save one JSON file per document:
{document_id, author_model: "gpt-6-luna", questions: [...]}
Use only the saved fulltext as evidence. Quotes may retain PDF wrapping or ligatures;
alignment allows whitespace and Unicode NFKC normalization, never fuzzy matching.
Evidence must include the relevant numbers/formulas/facts, not just a sentence intro.
Full sentences or paragraphs are acceptable. Validate all quotes with evidence_span
from evaluate.py; repair any failure before considering a document complete.

Root assigns balanced gold positions deterministically without changing option
content. Gold answers, evidence, and rationales are never included in judge prompts.
Judge evaluation proceeds while authors are still producing other papers' questions.
Question/option/gold changes invalidate that paper's checkpoint; evidence-only edits
do not change judge inputs and can be merged without repeating inference.
prompts.note: Saved task protocol for gpt-6-luna authors. Per-document assignments and subsequent review dialogue are not a fully archived agent transcript. Reuse frozen QA for exact comparison.

prompts.title: A12. Exact historical sanitizer and choice parser
prompts.text:
def historical_sanitize(value: str) -> str:
    """Reproduce the legacy ASCII filter applied by the MCQ answering wrapper."""
    allowed_special_chars = r"\.,\-\+\\/\*%$!?[\]\(\){}"
    pattern = r"[^a-zA-Z0-9\s{}]".format(allowed_special_chars)
    return re.sub(pattern, "", value)

def extract_historical_choice(response: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Reproduce the paper evaluator's semicolon-split answer extraction.

    The original implementation split the response on semicolons and selected
    the first field whose stripped value was exactly A, B, C, or D. This also
    accepts one-sided delimiters such as ``C;`` and ``;C`` without accepting a
    letter embedded in free-form prose.
    """
    for field in response.split(";"):
        choice = field.strip()
        if choice in {"A", "B", "C", "D"}:
            return choice
    return None
prompts.note: Executable definitions, not model prompts. Included because punctuation removal changes the effective student input.
